ruling.explanation:
Decision on trip TRP-00104 (Tampines Hub to one-north), for both parties.

WHAT THE TRACE SHOWS. The GPS trace measures 34.17 km and that is the figure that governs the threshold test (POL-RD-01; the trip record's 34.2 km is a rounded copy and may not be cited). The booked optimal route was 27.1 km. The excess is 7.07 km, or 26.09% of optimal, which clears both POL-RD-01 gates (more than 20% and more than 0.8 km), so the deviation is established on this trip's own measurement. It does not reach either materiality marker (50% or 8.0 km), so POL-RD-06 is not engaged; and in any event the driver's trailing-90-day record is 1 flag in 288 completed trips, far below the pattern thresholds, so no full-refund uplift and no driver-conduct referral can follow. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is context only and is not substituted. The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes (283 fixes, 10-second sampling, 100% coverage, no gaps), so POL-RD-07's corroboration rule and the POL-RD-10(3) escalation route are not open, and the excess is measured directly.

THE DRIVER'S EXONERATION. POL-RD-03 applies. LTA advisory ADV-20260716-007 (HIGH severity, two of three lanes blocked) names the PIE towards Tuas after Eunos Link exit, which is the corridor the optimal route uses, and its 20:02-21:35 window overlaps the trip; the route left that corridor before the affected segment and rejoined it. The driver was right to avoid the accident and is not fined for it. But the exoneration is capped: justified excess = min(7.07, 1.30 x (30.1 - 27.1) + 1.00) = 4.90 km. The driver's own trace, 34.17 km, is 4.07 km longer than the 30.1 km shortest lawful alternative the advisory made available; that mileage is the driver's choice, not the accident's. The second advisory (ADV-20260716-055, CTE towards SLE, intersects_route false) exonerates nothing: it covers a corridor the optimal route never uses.

THE REFUND. The closure-adjusted optimal is 27.1 + 4.90 = 32.00 km, with duration scaled from the booked 34.0 to 40.1 minutes. recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 32.00 + 0.28 x 40.1) x 1.0 (surge read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP = 39.828. Refund = 43.41 charged_total - 39.828 = 3.582, rounded up to SGD 3.60. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and far below 90% of the fare, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND. Charged_total 43.41, recomputed_fare 39.828 and refund 3.60 are the three lines.

ON THE DRIVER'S "NO ACTION" ARGUMENT. I do not accept that the 2.17 km residue fails POL-RD-01 and leaves the whole charge standing. POL-RD-03 states expressly that excess beyond the cap is not exonerated and IS refunded under POL-RD-02 computed against the closure-adjusted optimal route, and POL-RD-02 directs its computation onto the adjusted route wherever POL-RD-03 excuses part of the excess. The 2.17 km is the part no closure explains, and it is refunded. The driver's fallback figure of a 3.60 ceiling is therefore right; his primary request that nothing be refunded is not.

ON THE RIDER'S ALTERNATIVE FIGURE. The SGD 9.00 computed on the unadjusted 27.1 km / 34.0 min baseline is not available: the POL-RD-03 exoneration is made out on the cited advisory, its window and the route geometry, so the refund runs on the adjusted baseline, not the booked one. The rider's sense that 43.41 is about 14.00 more than usual is not the measure the policy uses.

OTHER CLAUSES. POL-RD-04 does not apply: the reroute was the driver's own proposal ('accident on PIE after eunos, i go ECP instead ok'); the rider's 'ok but not too long ah' is not an instruction naming a road or place, and waypoint_hint is null, so no rider-requested detour is made out and no excess is excluded on that ground. POL-RD-05 does not open (no amended pickup or dropoff, no amended optimal stored). POL-RD-11 does not apply: the fare model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so the distance-and-time refund route is not closed. POL-RD-09 adds nothing: erp_gantries is empty, the off-route ERP total is 0.00, and there is no airport surcharge, so there is no pass-through correction and no billing-integrity referral. POL-RD-08 is satisfied on both sides as described, and the rider's profile does not trigger the extra-corroboration rule. The charge is live (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued 0.00).

Both parties' profiles were used only to weight credibility; no context-only field (ratings, acceptance rate, account age, lifetime counters, prior disputes) has been used to decide anything about this trip.

No mandatory escalation applies: confidence is above the 0.70 floor, the trip identifiers match, the trace is unimpaired, no timestamps conflict, no exculpatory clause was invoked against a missing or inapplicable artifact, and the refund is well within the POL-RD-10(6) ceiling. Confidence 0.9, the cap being the full weight of the artifacts that carry the deciding facts.
